observation.visible_scene: A wide beach at sunset (or sunrise): a colorful sky with streaked orange, yellow, blue and purple clouds over a calm sea, with a glowing sun near the horizon at center-right. Two thin wave lines roll in the mid-distance, and a wet-sand foreground mirrors the sky's colors. The frame is essentially a fixed landscape view; the only activity is the surface water.
visible_changes: The sky, cloud shapes, sun glow and horizon line stay in the same positions across all frames (no visible cloud drift or sun movement within this ~2.7 s window).

The mid-distance wave crest lines keep roughly the same vertical position but their foam texture and broken segments change frame to frame, indicating small waves continuously breaking along those lines.

The near-shore foam edge oscillates slightly: its height and the width of the bright reflected band on the wet sand shift a few pixels between frames, consistent with a thin sheet of water advancing and receding rather than a single one-way motion.
The foreground reflection of the orange and blue sky ripples and reshapes as the water film on the sand moves; these bright patches are reflections on the wet sand, not separate standing pools.
No panning, zooming or tilt is evident: the horizon and cloud features remain fixed in the frame, so camera motion is absent or negligible.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the waves are generally building toward shore or draining back over a longer timescale (the segment shows only small oscillation).
Any change in sky color, sun position or cloud motion outside this short window.
Wind, tide, or any person/animal that may be present beyond the cropped frame.
uncertain_details: The exact propagation direction of each wave line is hard to confirm from texture changes alone.
Minor pixel-level differences in the near-shore foam line could be wave motion or just changing foam pattern; a clear net translation is not established.
Camera is treated as static based on fixed background, but sub-pixel drift cannot be fully ruled out.
